item.title: Oil Prices Fall for Third Day as Saudi Supply Concerns Ease Slightly
item.description: Oil prices fell for a third day Friday, with WTI crude slipping below $100 a barrel as expectations of restored Saudi pipeline flows eased immediate supply concerns.

item.description: Russia also placed the local businesses of French retailers Auchan and Leroy Merlin under temporary external administration, according to a presidential decree.

item.title: Bank of Japan Raises Rates, Making U.S. Less Alluring for Tokyo Investors
item.description: The yen weakened as two members of the bank’s board suggested future rate rises might come more slowly than anticipated.

item.title: Malaysia’s Former Prime Minister Can Serve Rest of 1MDB Sentence Under House Arrest
item.description: The royal pardon for Najib Razak marks the latest chapter in one of the largest financial crimes of the century.

item.title: North Korea Sends Women to Russian Factories in Line of Ukrainian Fire
item.description: Kim Jong Un has deployed factory crews into an expanding war zone to bolster ties with President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: The U.S. and China Want AI Guardrails. But Their Ideas Couldn’t Be More Different.
item.description: American dialogue has centered on protecting humanity from the technology, while Beijing is chiefly concerned with safeguarding the Communist Party.

item.title: Stellantis Could Face Strike Threat in Canada Over Factory Sale
item.description: The union representing more than 9,000 Stellantis employees in Canada said it could be in a strike position in the coming weeks unless the carmaker changes course on its plan to sell a Toronto-area factory to a defense firm.

item.title: Crude Oil Futures Post Back-to Back Losses

item.description: WSJ’s Shelby Holliday explains how the Houthis pulled off a swift offensive that has sparked fighting and sent oil prices soaring.

item.title: Why the Bank of England Didn’t Follow the Fed in Raising Interest Rates
item.description: The U.K. central bank is monitoring for signs that higher energy costs are spilling over into everyday prices.

item.description: Under formally presented new rules, social networks could be required to use age verification tools to stop under 15s creating their own accounts, and children under 13 would be banned from accessing social media.
